cancer_indication: FDA-approved for HER2-negative breast cancers in both metastatic and early-stage (adjuvant) settings, contingent on a deleterious germline BRCA1/2 mutation; used after standard therapies (including chemotherapy, and endocrine therapy if ER-positive).
drug_class: PARP inhibitor (PARP1/2 inhibitor; PARP3 minor target)
moa: Inhibits PARP1 and PARP2 catalytic activity and traps PARP1 on DNA, impairing base-excision/single-strand break repair; unrepaired SSBs convert into DSBs during replication, which become lethal in tumors with homologous recombination repair defects (synthetic lethality), driving apoptosis and growth arrest in HRD/BRCA-mutant breast cancers.

REACTOME_HOMOLOGOUS_RECOMBINATION.description: High-fidelity double-strand break repair pathway requiring BRCA1/BRCA2 and other HR factors (e.g., RAD51) to repair replication-associated DNA damage.
REACTOME_HOMOLOGOUS_RECOMBINATION.interpretation: Olaparib's therapeutic rationale in breast cancer is strongly tied to tumors with homologous recombination repair dysfunction (HRD) and the capacity (or lack thereof) to resolve DSBs created downstream of PARP inhibition; tumors can evolve adaptations that restore HR capacity.

REACTOME_NONHOMOLOGOUS_END_JOINING_NHEJ.description: Error-prone DSB repair pathway influenced by 53BP1/RIF1/Shieldin-mediated control of DNA end resection and pathway choice between NHEJ vs HR.
REACTOME_NONHOMOLOGOUS_END_JOINING_NHEJ.interpretation: Alterations in NHEJ pathway components can shift repair pathway choice and modulate the functional HR state in BRCA1-deficient contexts, impacting how tumors tolerate DNA lesions associated with PARP inhibition.

HALLMARK_PI3K_AKT_MTOR_SIGNALING.description: Core growth/survival signaling axis (PI3K→AKT→mTOR) that promotes cellular survival programs and can influence DNA-damage tolerance and repair-associated transcriptional states.
HALLMARK_PI3K_AKT_MTOR_SIGNALING.interpretation: This pathway is relevant to breast-cancer cell survival under genotoxic stress and is discussed as a compensatory survival network in the setting of PARP inhibition, providing rationale for combination strategies that co-target PI3K/AKT signaling in selected contexts.

HALLMARK_INTERFERON_ALPHA_RESPONSE.description: Type I interferon gene program reflecting innate immune activation, including interferon-stimulated genes downstream of cGAS-STING signaling.
HALLMARK_INTERFERON_ALPHA_RESPONSE.interpretation: PARP inhibitor-associated DNA damage can engage innate immune sensing pathways and Type I interferon signaling, supporting immune-mediated tumor control and providing rationale for combinations involving immunotherapy or STING-pathway activation (notably highlighted in BRCA-associated breast cancer models).

REACTOME_ABCFAMILY_PROTEINS_MEDIATED_TRA.description: ATP-binding cassette (ABC) transporter-mediated drug transport/efflux processes (e.g., ABCB1/P-gp, ABCG2) that reduce intracellular exposure to substrates.
REACTOME_ABCFAMILY_PROTEINS_MEDIATED_TRA.interpretation: Drug-efflux mechanisms are a key pharmacologic determinant of tumor drug exposure and are highlighted as an important resistance-related process that can also drive cross-resistance with other agents.

REACTOME_ACTIVATION_OF_ATR_IN_RESPONSE_T.description: Replication-stress response pathway centered on ATR-dependent checkpoint signaling (including CHK1) that stabilizes stalled replication forks and coordinates cell-cycle arrest/repair.
REACTOME_ACTIVATION_OF_ATR_IN_RESPONSE_T.interpretation: Because PARP inhibition induces replication stress and DNA lesions, ATR-mediated checkpoint activation is a major tumor stress-response pathway discussed in the report as relevant to how tumor cells survive ongoing DNA damage and as a combination target (e.g., ATR/DDR inhibition strategies).

HALLMARK_APOPTOSIS.description: Programmed cell-death execution programs, including intrinsic apoptotic priming and pro-apoptotic effectors (e.g., BAX, PUMA, BIM) downstream of DNA damage signaling.
HALLMARK_APOPTOSIS.interpretation: The report frames apoptosis competence as an important determinant of whether PARP-inhibitor-induced DNA damage culminates in irreversible tumor cell death, with subtype context noted (e.g., functional p53 in some ER+ settings; alternative death routes in p53-mutant tumors).

HALLMARK_P53_PATHWAY.description: p53-mediated DNA damage response program integrating checkpoint control and apoptosis induction following genotoxic stress.
HALLMARK_P53_PATHWAY.interpretation: The report emphasizes p53 pathway status as relevant to how tumors respond to accumulated DNA damage (cell-cycle arrest vs apoptosis vs tolerance), noting that p53 loss is common in TNBC and can influence damage tolerance and evolutionary routes under treatment pressure.

REACTOME_FANCONI_ANEMIA_PATHWAY.description: Fanconi anemia DNA repair network that resolves interstrand crosslinks and interfaces with homologous recombination processes (e.g., via FANCA/FANCD2 and related factors).
REACTOME_FANCONI_ANEMIA_PATHWAY.interpretation: FA pathway integrity is discussed as relevant to broader DNA repair vulnerability states in breast cancer (HRD/DDR deficiency contexts) that intersect with PARP inhibitor mechanisms.

REACTOME_BASE_EXCISION_REPAIR.description: Base excision repair/single-strand break repair processes in which PARP1/2 detect DNA damage and recruit repair factors via PARylation.
REACTOME_BASE_EXCISION_REPAIR.interpretation: This is the direct mechanistic repair pathway perturbed by olaparib through PARP1/2 inhibition and PARP trapping, linking upstream repair blockade to downstream accumulation of cytotoxic lesions in susceptible tumor contexts.

Breast_cancer_subtype_information.description: Highlighted as the archetype of responsiveness in the report: BRCA-mutant TNBC is emphasized as inherently HR-deficient, with olaparib inducing profound DNA damage, apoptosis, and growth arrest. The report also notes subtype-specific immune context where BRCA-mutant TNBC can show stronger cGAS-STING/Type I interferon signaling and immune recruitment, supporting response and combination rationale. It additionally notes TP53 pathway suppression is common in TNBC and can affect damage tolerance/evolution under PARP inhibition.

Breast_cancer_subtype_information.subtype: HR+/HER2- (Luminal; including BRCA2-mutant and selected luminal B with HRD)
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.description: The report states hormone receptor-positive HER2-negative cancers with BRCA2 mutations can benefit, while ER+/HER2- tumors without HRD are inherently insensitive. It also describes that luminal tumors may be more immunologically “cold,” potentially limiting benefit from IFN/immune-inflammatory mechanisms relative to TNBC.

The report indicates that HER2+ tumors without HRD essentially do not benefit and are not indicated. It separately notes that some HER2+ tumors with high TILs could potentially exploit immune-inflammatory signaling pathways in the context of combination strategies, but HRD remains central for benefit.

Across subtypes, the report emphasizes olaparib as targeted therapy for the DNA repair-defective subset (germline BRCA1/2-mutant; broader HRD/BRCAness contexts). It states FDA approval in HER2-negative metastatic and adjuvant early-stage settings contingent on deleterious BRCA mutation and describes guideline-driven patient selection via germline BRCA testing.

notes: Some pathway labels in the report appear in closely related naming forms (e.g., ATR/CHK1 checkpoint signaling for ATR replication-stress response; Fanconi anemia/DNA crosslink repair for FA pathway; PARP1-BER/Base excision repair for BER; TP53 pathway for p53). Safety/contraindications noted in the report include no absolute FDA contraindications beyond hypersensitivity, with breastfeeding contraindicated per EMA and practical avoidance in pregnancy; caution/avoidance in severe renal/hepatic impairment and with strong CYP3A4 modulators.
